newsitem.title: UK: DMG New York loss less than reported - sources.
newsitem.headline: DMG New York loss less than reported - sources.

text.p: Trading losses at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell's New York office, reported in a British newspaper on Sunday, are not expected to total more than 10 million pounds ($16.3 million), banking industry sources said on Monday.
The Observer newspaper said the investment banking arm of Germany's Deutsche Bank's had sustained losses "as a result of a difference of opinion over a valuation" in equity derivatives.

The paper said DMG officials in New York had said the losses were "not material". It said a trader from the equities derivatives team there resigned last month but was not suspected of having acted dishonestly or for personal gain.
Banking sources said the book losses had not been realised and were not expected to be more than a "single digit million" figure, representing a normal trading loss for the investment bank.

DMG is expected to be punished shortly by British investments watchdog the Investment Management Regulatory Organisation (IMRO) for failings in its fund management arm Morgan Grenfell Asset Management (MGAM) following the revelation last September of irregularities in three of its funds.

Deutsche Bank last month estimated that the MGAM affair could cost it some 430 million pounds. It made a 180 million pound cash injection to the funds last September and has since said it would pay around 200 million pounds in compensation to investors.
